## Investigation Summary

Your right-click menu disappearing at the bottom of the screen is a **known tmux design issue** with menu positioning. Here are the exact sources:

### 1. Right-Click Pane Menu Binding
**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` **Lines 12–39**

The pane right-click uses:
```tmux
bind-key -n MouseDown3Pane \
  if-shell -F -t = "#{||:#{mouse_any_flag},#{&&:#{pane_in_mode},#{?#{m/r:(copy|view)-mode,#{pane_mode}},0,1}}}" \
    { select-pane -t = ; send-keys -M } \
    { display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{pane_current_command} (pane #{pane_index})" -t = -x M -y M \
        ... 30+ menu items ...
```

**Key issue:** `-x M -y M` — both coordinates are anchored to the **mouse position**. When you right-click near the bottom, `M` resolves to a low y-coordinate, and tmux's auto-clamping in 3.3+ may suppress the entire menu if it would extend past the terminal height.

**Window-tab menu** (line 55) uses `-x W -y W` (window position), and **session menu** (line 77) uses `-x M -y W` (mixed anchors).

### 2. Known Menu Positioning Bug
**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md`

Documents two distinct failures:
- **Mouse-release dismiss:** nested submenus flash and disappear because pending mouse events from the parent right-click dismiss them (even with `-O` flag).
- **Bottom-right corner placement:** `-y P` (pane line) from a status-bar event resolves to the status bar row (bottom of terminal), gluing the menu to bottom-right.

**Workaround applied in your config:** Lines 44–50 of `keybindings.conf` explicitly inline all layout commands into the window-tab menu instead of nesting via `run-shell`, to avoid this exact bug.

### 3. Menu-Too-Tall Silent Suppression
**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`

- **Root cause:** `display-menu` silently suppresses the entire popup if menu height exceeds available terminal height after `status-position` and `-y` offset. No error, no log entry — "if the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed" per `man tmux`.
- **Your config workaround:** `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh` reads `#{client_height}` and emits three tiers (14 rows max for top menu) so it always fits even on mobile SSH.

### 4. Version Constraint & AppImage
**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` **Lines 1884–2000+**

- **Minimum tmux version:** 3.3 (line 1925: `tmux_min_version: "3.3"`)
- **Reason:** tmux 3.2a silently suppresses menus positioned past terminal right edge; 3.3 introduced position clamping and arithmetic in `-x`/`-y`.
- **AppImage fallback:** If Linuxbrew unavailable on x86_64, downloads `nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage` and installs a shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux`.

### 5. Documentation
**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md` **Lines 149–161**

Explicitly states the pane menu uses `display-menu -O` so it stays open after mouse release (tmux defaults omit `-O` and dismiss immediately, making right-click menus "unusable").

---

**Diagnosis for your bug:** When right-clicking near the bottom, `-x M -y M` places the menu anchor at the mouse (low y). If the 30-row pane menu would extend below the terminal, tmux 3.3+ clamps it, but the bottom-pinned anchor may cause the menu to render off-screen or collapse. Check: (1) terminal height `echo $LINES`, (2) tmux version `tmux -V`, (3) try right-clicking higher where there's more space below the click point.

267	# prefix + B : break current pane into a new window AND move it to a target
268	#              session in one go (acts like dragging a tab out).
269	# prefix + A : link current window into another session (window appears in
270	#              both sessions; edit either, both update). Use prefix + & to
271	#              kill, or unlink-window to detach without killing.
272	#
273	# Cross-window pane operations (no top-level prefix binding — letter slots are
274	# saturated by resize-pane H/J/K/L and sesh-last S; pane join/send live in the
275	# right-click pane menu and the popup menu's Session submenu instead):
276	#   - Mark current pane:  prefix + m  (built-in)
277	#   - Pull marked pane:   right-click pane menu → "Join marked pane here"
278	#   - Push current pane:  right-click pane menu → "Send pane to..."
279	#   - Break out to new window: right-click pane menu → "Break to new window"
280	#                              or prefix + ! (built-in, same session)
281	#                              or prefix + B (break + move to chosen session)
282	
283	bind M run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
284	  display-message "Pick destination session to MOVE window into…" \; \
285	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
286	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh move %%'"
287	bind B run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_pane '#{pane_id}'" \; \
288	  display-message "Pick destination session to BREAK pane into (as new window)…" \; \
289	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
290	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh break %%'"
291	bind A run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
292	  display-message "Pick destination session to LINK window into (window lives in both)…" \; \
293	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
294	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh link %%'"
295	
296	# prefix + E : explode — break EVERY pane in current window into its own window
297	#              within the SAME session. Use case: switching from wide screen
298	#              (multi-pane layout) to mobile/SSH where one pane per window is
299	#              easier than zooming with prefix + z. Source window keeps the
300	#              first pane; other panes become sibling windows inserted right
301	#              after it, named after each pane's current command.
302	bind E run-shell "~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh"
303	
304	# =============================================================================
305	# Theme Switching (Catppuccin <-> tmux2k)
306	# =============================================================================
307	# Note: first-time switch requires `prefix + I` to install the target plugin.
308	
309	bind M-c run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant catppuccin; \
310	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
311	  tmux display-message 'Theme: catppuccin'"
312	
313	bind M-t run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \
314	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
315	  tmux display-message 'Theme: tmux2k'"
316	
317	# =============================================================================
318	# Sesh (tmux session manager)
319	# =============================================================================
320	
321	# prefix + g: sesh picker in a tmux popup with fzf
322	bind-key "g" run-shell "sesh connect \"$(\
323	  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
324	    --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
325	    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
326	    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
327	    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
328	    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
329	    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
330	    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
331	    --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
332	    --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
333	    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
334	    --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
335	)\""
336	
337	bind -N "last-session (via sesh)" S run-shell "sesh last 2>/dev/null || tmux display-message 'No previous sesh session'"
338	
339	# prefix + 9: open repo-aware coding-agent layout (`scode`) for the current
340	# pane's directory. scode walks up from cwd to find .git; if not in a repo,
341	# the error surfaces in the tmux status line.
342	# Replaces the previous `sesh connect --root $(pwd)` binding (which had a
343	# subtle bug — $(pwd) was expanded once at config parse time, not per-press).
344	# Logic is in scode-here.sh because tmux run-shell is /bin/sh (can't see
345	# zsh functions) and the session-name + switch-client dance is non-trivial.
346	bind -N "scode for current dir (repo-aware coding layout)" 9 \
347	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/scode-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
348	
349	# prefix + 0: lightweight counterpart to prefix+9. Plain sesh session at
350	# the git root of the current pane's directory (no nvim/agent layout).
351	# Replaces tmux's built-in `select-window -t :=0` which always errored
352	# because base-index is 1 (no window 0 exists). Logic in sesh-root-here.sh
353	# — see that file for the two bugs in the original `sesh connect --root
354	# $(pwd)` binding (parse-time $(pwd) + misuse of --root flag).
355	bind -N "sesh-root for current dir (lightweight)" 0 \
356	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
357	
358	# prefix + T: sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup
359	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
360	
361	# prefix + O: sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup
362	bind-key "O" display-popup -h 90% -w 50% -E "sesh picker -i"
363	
364	# prefix + U: CLI tools picker via television (tv tools)
365	bind-key "U" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' CLI Tools (tv) ' "tv tools"
366	
367	# prefix + a: live coding-agent panes picker (tv agent-panes)
368	# Shows claude / cursor-agent / codex / opencode sessions currently running in
369	# any tmux pane. Enter switches focus to that pane. See:
370	#   docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md
371	bind-key "a" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Live agent panes (tv) ' "tv agent-panes"
372	
373	# (prefix + W is now bound earlier in this file as `kill-window`. The previous
374	# `sesh window` binding was removed because `sesh` has no `window` subcommand;
375	# pressing it printed sesh's help to a popup. See git history.)
376	
377	# =============================================================================
378	# Popup tools (display-popup -E -d '#{pane_current_path}')
379	# =============================================================================
380	# Floating scratch pane (tmux-floax) is on prefix + F (toggleable, persistent
381	# session named `float`). The bindings below are one-shot popups that close
382	# when the inner command exits — handy for "do one thing without disrupting
383	# the layout" workflows.
384	
385	# prefix + G: lazygit popup at current pane path
386	bind-key "G" display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' "lazygit"
387	
388	# prefix + ` (backtick): one-shot popup shell at current pane path.
389	# Closes when the inner shell exits (`exit` or Ctrl-D). Each invocation gets
390	# a fresh shell — no state preserved. For a persistent scratchpad with
391	# history, use floax (prefix + F) instead.
392	bind-key '`' display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' shell '
393	
394	# =============================================================================
395	# Help / cheatsheet
396	# =============================================================================
397	# tmux's built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys -N) is hard to scan and can't search
398	# user-defined bindings well. We replace it with tmux-fzf's keybinding picker
399	# (fzf popup, fuzzy-searchable). The original list-keys is still reachable on
400	# `prefix + C-?` as a fallback.
401	#
402	# `prefix + /` (built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to) is left
403	# alone — it's already useful for "what does THIS key do?" lookups.
404	#
405	# `?` inside the prefix + Enter popup menu opens a glow-rendered
406	# cheatsheet (curated, grouped, prettier than list-keys).
407	
408	unbind-key '?'
409	bind-key '?' run-shell -b "~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/main.sh"
410	bind-key 'C-?' list-keys -N
411	
412	# `/` inside the Enter-popup uses this; standalone prefix + / stays built-in
413	# (key-prompt). We expose the cheatsheet through the popup menu's `?` entry.
414	bind-key M-/ display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' \
415	  "glow -p ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null \
416	    || less ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md"
417	
418	# =============================================================================
419	# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
420	# =============================================================================
421	# Two entry keys, same menu. The menu itself is generated by a script
422	# (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) which:
423	#
424	#   1. Reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list. tmux's
425	#      `display-menu` does NOT paginate — if the menu is taller than the
426	#      terminal, the entire popup is silently suppressed (no error). The
427	#      script keeps the menu fitting on tiny mobile-SSH heights too.
428	#   2. Submenus are sibling scripts (menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh,
429	#      menu-sesh.sh, menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh). Each
430	#      `exec tmux display-menu …` so quoting context resets per submenu —
431	#      no nested-quote escaping disasters in keybindings.conf.
432	#
433	# History: an earlier flat ~50-row menu silently failed on smaller heights
434	# and was misdiagnosed as a csi-u key encoding bug, then as a quoting bug.
435	# Both real (the `\;` accelerator was broken, sesh fzf binds had nested-
436	# quote issues), but the dominant symptom — "menu doesn't open at all" —
437	# was actually menu-too-tall. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
438	#
439	# Discovery fallbacks if you forget the keys: `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf fuzzy
440	# picker over every binding), `prefix + M-/` (glow cheatsheet popup), or
441	# right-click on a pane / status line.
442	
443	unbind-key Space
444	unbind-key Enter
445	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
446	# Note: `prefix + e` was previously a popup-menu alias (added as workaround
447	# for a misdiagnosed display-menu bug — see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
448	# Removed so `e` is free as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal"
449	# in the window right-click menu).
450

```text
1	# tmux — Keybindings
2	
3	All bindings use the default prefix `Ctrl + b`.
4	
5	## Daily Workflow
6	
7	| Keybinding | Action |
8	|------------|--------|
9	| `prefix + R` | Reload `~/.tmux.conf` |
10	| `prefix + Space` | Open the tmux popup menu (mnemonic: "menu") |
11	| `prefix + g` | Open sesh picker |
12	| `prefix + T` | Open sesh picker via television (tv) |
13	| `prefix + O` | Open sesh built-in picker |
14	| `prefix + S` | Jump to the last sesh session (status-bar message if none) |
15	| `prefix + 9` | Open `scode` for current dir (repo-aware coding-agent layout — nvim 75% \| agent 25% + btop monitor; idempotent, switches to existing session if already created) |
16	| `prefix + 0` | Lightweight sesh session at git root of current dir (no nvim/agent layout — symmetric counterpart to `prefix + 9`) |
17	| `prefix + N` | New session (prompts for name) |
18	| `prefix + X` | Kill session (with confirmation) |
19	| `prefix + W` | Kill window (with confirmation) |
20	| `prefix + r` | Renumber windows (close gaps left by killed windows) |
21	| `prefix + M` | Move current window to another session (prompts for `session[:index]`) |
22	| `prefix + B` | Break current pane into a new window and move it to a session (tab tear-out) |
23	| `prefix + A` | Link current window into another session (window appears in both) |
24	| `prefix + E` | Explode — break every pane in current window into its own window (same session). For switching from wide-screen multi-pane to mobile/SSH single-pane |
25	| `prefix + d` | Detach |
26	| `prefix + t` | Show tmux clock mode |
27	| `prefix + M-c` | Switch theme to Catppuccin (top status bar) |
28	| `prefix + M-t` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |
29	
30	## Panes and Windows
31	
32	| Keybinding | Action |
33	|------------|--------|
34	| `Ctrl + 1..9` | Switch to window 1–9 (requires CSI-u terminal: Ghostty, Alacritty, Kitty) |
35	| `Ctrl + 0` | Lightweight sesh session at repo root for current pane (mirrors `prefix + 0`) |
36	| `Ctrl + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes — crosses into Neovim splits (vim-tmux-navigator) |
37	| `Ctrl + \` | Focus previous pane/split (vim-tmux-navigator) |
38	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes (fallback, tmux-only) |
39	| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells, repeatable) |
40	| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell, repeatable) |
41	| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
42	| `prefix + \|` | Split left/right (vertical divider) |
43	| `prefix + -` | Split top/bottom (horizontal divider) |
44	| `prefix + c` | New window in current path |
45	| `prefix + x` | Kill pane (with confirmation) |
46	| `prefix + W` | Kill window (with confirmation) |
47	| `prefix + r` | Manually renumber windows (close index gaps) |
48	| `prefix + z` | Toggle pane zoom |
49	| `prefix + {` | Swap pane with previous (left/up) |
50	| `prefix + }` | Swap pane with next (right/down) |
51	| `prefix + m` | **Mark** current pane (built-in; one mark globally; needed by Join in menus) |
52	| `prefix + !` | Break current pane into a new window in same session (built-in) |
53	| `prefix + [` | Enter copy mode |
54	
55	`Ctrl+1..9` and `Ctrl+0` require CSI-u terminal support. Ghostty/cmux sends these natively. Alacritty needs explicit `keyboard.bindings` (managed by this repo in `dot_config/alacritty/alacritty.toml`). Legacy terminals (Terminal.app, plain SSH) cannot send these — use `prefix + number` instead.
56	
57	Swap-pane swaps the **content** while keeping the **sizes**. So if you have a 75%/25% split and swap, the left pane's content moves to the right (25%) and vice versa — the proportions stay fixed.
58	
59	## Layouts
60	
61	| Keybinding | Action |
62	|------------|--------|
63	| `M-1` | Even horizontal layout |
64	| `M-2` | Even vertical layout |
65	| `M-3` | Main horizontal layout |
66	| `M-4` | Main vertical layout |
67	| `M-5` | Tiled layout |
68	| `prefix + E` | Spread panes evenly (built-in) |
69	
70	`M-1` through `M-5` are tmux built-ins — no prefix needed; just hold Meta (Alt/Option) and press the number.
71	
72	> **macOS terminal requirement**: Option must send Meta/Esc+ for `M-` bindings to work. Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed by this repo in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). Alacritty: `window.option_as_alt: OnlyLeft`. iTerm2: Profiles > Keys > Left Option Key > Esc+. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](../ghostty.md).
73	
74	## Floating Pane (tmux-floax)
75	
76	| Keybinding | Action |
77	|------------|--------|
78	| `prefix + F` | Toggle floating pane (80% width/height, **persistent** `float` session) |
79	| `prefix + P` | Open floax popup menu |
80	| `prefix + \`` | One-shot **popup shell** at current pane path (each invocation = fresh shell, exits on `exit`/Ctrl-D) |
81	
82	Two flavours of popup shell, pick by use case:
83	
84	- **`prefix + \``** — quick-and-forget. Run a `curl`, check `df -h`, eyeball a file, exit. Each open is a clean shell. No history across opens. Good for "I just need to type one command without leaving my pane layout".
85	- **`prefix + F` (floax)** — scratchpad. The `float` session persists, so when you re-toggle the popup, your previous shell history, environment, and even running processes are still there. Good for "I'm iterating on something and don't want to lose the context".
86	
87	## One-shot Popups
88	
89	These open `display-popup -E` at `#{pane_current_path}`; the popup closes when the inner command exits. Unlike floax, no session persists.
90	
91	| Keybinding | Action |
92	|------------|--------|
93	| `prefix + G` | [`lazygit`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit) popup |
94	| `prefix + T` | sesh picker (television) |
95	| `prefix + O` | sesh built-in picker |
96	| `prefix + U` | CLI tools picker (`tv tools`) |
97	| `prefix + u` | URL picker (tmux-fzf-url) |
98	| `prefix + a` | Live coding-agent panes picker (`tv agent-panes`) — see [agent pane discovery](../agent-panes-discovery.md) |
99	
100	When to use which:
101	
102	- **floax (`prefix + F`)** — repeated quick-access shell, want history preserved (notes, scratch math, long-running curl).
103	- **`prefix + \`` popup shell** — quick command in a fresh shell, exit and forget.
104	- **One-shot tool popup (`G`/...)** — start a TUI tool, do work, exit cleanly.
105	
106	## Help / Discovery (no more memorizing)
107	
108	The built-in `prefix + ?` (a wall-of-text `list-keys -N` dump) is replaced with [tmux-fzf](https://github.com/sainnhe/tmux-fzf): an fzf popup over **every** binding (including user-defined), fully fuzzy-searchable.
109	
110	| Keybinding | Action |
111	|------------|--------|
112	| `prefix + ?` | tmux-fzf: top-level fuzzy picker (keybindings / sessions / windows / panes / commands / processes / clipboard) |
113	| `prefix + C-?` | Plain `list-keys -N` (fallback if tmux-fzf is missing) |
114	| `prefix + /` | Built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to (single-key lookup) |
115	| `prefix + Space` then `?` | Curated cheatsheet rendered with [`glow`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glow) (source: `dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md`) |
116	| `prefix + Space` then `/` | tmux-fzf **keybinding** picker directly (skips the category menu) |
117	
118	Three layers of "I forgot the key" recovery:
119	
120	1. **Curated** (`prefix + Space`): grouped popup menu with the high-traffic top-level rows + submenus.
121	2. **Searchable** (`prefix + ?` → tmux-fzf): fuzzy-search across the full binding list.
122	3. **Reference** (`prefix + Space` → `?`): glow-rendered markdown cheatsheet (this file's `cheatsheet.md` sibling), good for browsing while learning.
123	
124	Why three? The popup menu is fastest once you know roughly what you want; tmux-fzf is for "I know it exists somewhere"; the cheatsheet is for "what's even possible?". Pick whichever matches your current uncertainty.
125	
126	## Copy Mode (Vim-Style)
127	
128	Enter with `prefix + [`. Navigate with vim keys, then:
129	
130	| Key | Action |
131	|-----|--------|
132	| `v` | Begin character selection (visual mode) |
133	| `V` | Select entire line |
134	| `C-v` | Toggle rectangle/block selection |
135	| `y` | Yank selection to system clipboard |
136	| `/` | Search forward |
137	| `?` | Search backward |
138	| `n`/`N` | Next/previous search match |
139	| `g`/`G` | Jump to top/bottom |
140	| `C-u`/`C-d` | Half-page up/down |
141	| `{` / `}` | Jump to previous / next prompt (needs OSC 133 — see [OSC 133](./README.md#osc-133-command-boundary-navigation-warp-style)) |
142	| `M-[` / `M-]` | Jump to previous / next command **output** start (needs OSC 133) |
143	| `q` or `Escape` | Exit copy mode |
144	
145	Mouse drag in copy mode also copies to clipboard. Double-click selects a word.
146	
147	Command-boundary keys (`{` `}` `M-[` `M-]`) rely on OSC 133 markers emitted by `dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh`. In a pane running a non-zsh shell or one that opted out via `DISABLE_OSC133=1`, they are silent no-ops.
148	
149	## Right-click menus
150	
151	Right-click opens a context menu depending on where you click:
152	
153	| Target | Menu items |
154	|--------|------------|
155	| Pane body (`MouseDown3Pane`) | Split h/v, swap up/down/left/right, zoom, resize 75% / even, mark, swap marked, **join marked here (h/v)**, **send pane to window…**, **break to new window**, copy mode, respawn, kill |
156	| Window list (`MouseDown3Status`) | Swap left/right, move/link to session, **merge into other window as pane (h/v)**, **even layout (horizontal / vertical / tiled)**, kill window, **renumber windows**, rename, new window |
157	| Session area on the left (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`) | Next/prev/rename session, move current window, new session/window |
158	
159	Our bindings use `display-menu -O` so the menu stays open after the mouse button is released — pick an item or press Escape to dismiss. (tmux's defaults omit `-O` and dismiss on release, which makes the menu unusable.)
160	
161	After break / send / merge / join, a status-bar message reports what happened (e.g. `Broke pane out to window 4 (zsh)`, `Merged into 1`).
162	
163	## URL Opening
164	
165	| Keybinding | Action |
166	|------------|--------|
167	| `prefix + u` | Open fzf popup listing all URLs in the pane (tmux-fzf-url) |
168	
169	In copy-mode (after selecting text with `v`):
170	
171	| Key | Action |
172	|-----|--------|
173	| `o` | Open selected URL/file in default browser/app (tmux-open) |
174	| `C-o` | Open selection in `$EDITOR` |
175	| `S` | Search selection in Google (tmux-open, configurable via `@open-S`) |
176	
177	Typical workflow: `prefix + u` for quick URL browsing; `prefix + [` then select + `o` for precise URL opening.
178	
179	## Capture Pane
180	
181	| Keybinding | Action |
182	|------------|--------|
183	| `prefix + y` | Copy visible pane content to system clipboard |
184	| `prefix + Y` | Copy full scrollback to system clipboard |
185	| `prefix + C-y` | Open scrollback in fzf, select lines to copy (Tab=multi) |
186	| `prefix + M-y` | Copy **last command's output** to clipboard (Warp-style, needs OSC 133 — see [OSC 133](./README.md#osc-133-command-boundary-navigation-warp-style)) |
187	| `prefix + M-i` | Copy **last command's input line** (prompt + typed command) to clipboard (needs OSC 133) |
188	
189	Cross-platform: `pbcopy` on macOS, `xclip`/`xsel` on Linux. OSC 52 also works for the vim-style `y` yank (even over SSH).
190	
191	## Moving Windows / Panes Across Sessions
192	
193	Like dragging a browser tab into a new window — but tmux can do it at three different granularities (whole window, pane → new window, pane → existing window as split). All cross-session/cross-window targets are picked from a `choose-tree` picker (live preview, fuzzy-search), not typed into a prompt. See the [picker-over-prompt design rule](#design-note-pickers-over-prompts) below for why.
194	
195	### Window-level (whole tab)
196	
197	| Key | Underlying command | Effect |
198	|-----|-------------------|--------|
199	| `prefix + M` | `choose-tree -Zs … move-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%'` | **Cut** current window out of this session and **paste** into target (session picker) |
200	| `prefix + A` | `choose-tree -Zs … link-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%:'` | **Link** (not copy): same window appears in both sessions; edits stay in sync. `unlink-window` removes one side without killing |
201	| `prefix + W` | `kill-window` | Kill current window (with confirmation) |
202	| `prefix + r` | `move-window -r` | Renumber windows in current session — closes index gaps. `renumber-windows on` (set in `common.conf`) auto-renumbers when a whole window is destroyed, but kill-pane on multi-pane windows or shell-driven exits can still leave gaps; this binding is the manual top-up. |
203	
204	### Pane → new window
205	
206	| Key | Underlying command | Effect |
207	|-----|-------------------|--------|
208	| `prefix + !` | `break-pane` (built-in) | Break current pane into a new window in the **same** session |
209	| `prefix + B` | `choose-tree -Zs … break-pane -s '#{pane_id}' -t '%%'` | Break + move to chosen session in one step (tab tear-out, session picker) |
210	| `prefix + E` | `~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh` | **Explode** — break every pane in current window into its own window (same session). Source window keeps the first pane; others become sibling windows inserted right after, named after each pane's current command. Use case: continuing a wide-screen multi-pane layout on mobile/SSH where one pane per window is easier than zooming with `prefix + z`. Also available via right-click window menu → "Break all panes → windows". |
211	| Right-click pane → "Break to new window" | `break-pane` | Same as `prefix + !`, but reports the new window index in the status bar |
212	
213	### Pane → existing window (as a split)
214	
215	These all use tmux's `join-pane`, which moves a pane between windows. `join-pane` always operates on individual **panes**, not whole windows — there is no "merge two windows wholesale" command. The two-step "mark + join" idiom is the canonical workflow:
216	
217	1. Go to the **source** pane (the one you want to move).
218	2. Press `prefix + m` to **mark** it. tmux remembers exactly one marked pane globally; the marked pane gets a coloured border.
219	3. Switch to the **destination** window.
220	4. Right-click any pane → "Join marked pane here (h-split)" or "(v-split)". The marked pane jumps over and becomes a split.
221	
222	Alternative entry points to the same `join-pane` command:
223	
224	| From | Action | Effect |
225	|------|--------|--------|
226	| Right-click pane → "Join marked pane here (h/v-split)" | `join-pane -h` / `-v` | Pull the marked pane into this window as a split |
227	| Right-click pane → "Send pane to window…" | `choose-tree -Zw … join-pane -h -s '#{pane_id}' -t '%%'` | Push **this** pane out to another window as a split (no mark needed; pick target from window tree picker) |
228	| Right-click window tab → "Merge into other window (as pane, h/v-split)" | `choose-tree -Zw … join-pane -h -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%'` | Move this window's **active pane** into another window as a split. If the source window has only one pane, it disappears (effectively merging the whole window). With multiple panes, only the active one moves. |
229	| popup menu → Session → "Join marked here (h/v)" / "Send pane to…" | same as right-click | Same actions, keyboard-driven |
230	
231	> **Why no top-level `prefix +` key for join-pane / send-pane?** All single-letter capital slots are taken (`H/J/K/L` = resize, `S` = sesh-last, `W` = kill-window, `M/N/B/A` = window ops). Rather than rebind something else, these live in the right-click menus and the popup menu's Session submenu. The mark-and-join workflow is mostly mouse-friendly anyway.
232	
233	Tip: `prefix + s` (built-in choose-tree) shows live previews — handy for previewing sessions before invoking `M`/`B`/`A`, though those bindings now open their own pickers so the standalone preview is mostly for casual browsing.
234	
235	### Design note: pickers over prompts
236	
237	All cross-window/cross-session bindings in this repo use `choose-tree -Zw` (window picker) or `-Zs` (session picker), not `command-prompt`. Two reasons:
238	
239	1. **Correctness for `target-pane` commands**. tmux's `join-pane`, `swap-pane`, `move-pane` parse `-t TARGET` as a *pane* — a bare integer `N` means "pane index N in the *current* window", not "window N". Users typing `1` thinking "window 1" silently target the wrong pane (often the source pane itself, producing `Source and target panes must be different`). `choose-tree -Zw` returns `session:window`, which the parser unambiguously resolves to that window's active pane. Full debugging trail in [`pitfalls/tmux-join-pane-numeric-target-pane-not-window.md`](../../../pitfalls/tmux-join-pane-numeric-target-pane-not-window.md).
240	2. **UX**. Live preview, fuzzy-search, and zero memorisation of session names beat a free-form prompt even when both are technically safe (e.g. `move-window -t` accepts session-level targets without ambiguity).
241	
242	Source pane/window is always pinned with `-s '#{pane_id}'` or `-s '#{window_id}'` rather than relying on "current pane / current window" — `#{pane_id}` resolves at click time against the client's active pane, which may not be the right-clicked tab on status-bar menus.
243	
244	When adding a new keybinding/menu row that targets a window or session: reach for `choose-tree -Zw` / `-Zs` first; only fall back to `command-prompt` if no picker fits (free-form rename, brand-new session name, etc.).
245	
246	## Built-in tmux Keys Still Available
247	
248	| Keybinding | Action |
249	|------------|--------|
250	| `prefix + s` | Choose session tree |
251	| `prefix + w` | Choose window tree |
252	| `prefix + q` | Show pane numbers |
253	| `prefix + ,` | Rename window |
254	| `prefix + $` | Rename session |
255	| `prefix + ?` | tmux-fzf: fuzzy-search all keybindings (rebound from list-keys) |
256	| `prefix + C-?` | Built-in `list-keys -N` (fallback) |
257	| `prefix + /` | Prompt for a key and show what it is bound to |
258	
259	## Popup Menu (`prefix + Space`)
260	
261	The popup menu is bound to `prefix + Space` and is **generated by a script** (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) rather than defined inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two reasons:
262	
263	1. **Quoting**. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell one-liners, escaping in `keybindings.conf` was fragile and broke silently.
264	2. **Height-aware trimming**. `display-menu` does **not** paginate. If the menu is taller than the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. The script reads `#{client_height}` and emits one of three tier sets so the menu always fits.
265	
266	Tiers:
267	
268	| Terminal height | Top menu shows |
269	|-----------------|----------------|
270	| Any (Tier 0)    | Last window/pane, Choose win/sess, Pane #s, Sesh picker, Lazygit (~9 rows) |
271	| ≥ 14 (Tier 0+2) | + submenu launchers (`→ Layouts/Session/Sesh+/Popups/Theme/System`), Cheatsheet, Search keys |
272	| ≥ 22 (Tier 0+1+2) | + New window, Split `\|`/`-`, Zoom |
273	
274	Submenus are separate scripts (`menu-layouts.sh`, `menu-session.sh`, `menu-sesh.sh`, `menu-popups.sh`, `menu-theme.sh`, `menu-system.sh`), invoked from rows via `run-shell`. Each is an independent `display-menu` so quoting context resets.
275	
276	> **Historical note**: an earlier debugging round assumed `prefix + Space` and `prefix + Enter` were broken because of `extended-keys` / `csi-u` keysym encoding (tmux/tmux#4571, #4147, #4959, #4984), and the menu was moved to `prefix + e` as a workaround. That diagnosis was wrong. The actual failure was that the inline 50-row flat menu was **taller than the terminal**, and tmux silently suppresses oversized menus per `man tmux` ("If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."). Both `Space` and `Enter` were always bindable; the keysym story was a red herring. Full debugging trail in [`pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`](../../../pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md). The menu was bound to both `Space` (canonical) and `e` (alias) for a while; the `e` alias has since been **removed** to free `e` as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal" in the window right-click menu). The canonical binding stays on `prefix + Space`.
277	
278	### Top-menu accelerator keys
279	
280	Accelerator keys match the standalone `prefix + key` bindings wherever possible — pressing `c` inside the menu does the same thing as `prefix + c` outside it.
281	
282	| Key | Row | Tier |
283	|-----|-----|------|
284	| `Tab` | Last window | 0 |
285	| `P` | Last pane | 0 |
286	| `w` | Choose window tree | 0 |
287	| `s` | Choose session tree | 0 |
288	| `q` | Show pane numbers | 0 |
289	| `g` | Sesh picker | 0 |
290	| `G` | Lazygit popup | 0 |
291	| `c` | New window | 1 (h ≥ 22) |
292	| `\|` | Split left/right | 1 |
293	| `-` | Split top/bottom | 1 |
294	| `z` | Zoom toggle | 1 |
295	| `L` | → Layouts submenu | 2 (h ≥ 14) |
296	| `S` | → Session submenu | 2 |
297	| `E` | → Sesh+ submenu | 2 |
298	| `o` | → Popups submenu | 2 |
299	| `T` | → Theme submenu | 2 |
300	| `Y` | → System submenu | 2 |
301	| `?` | Glow cheatsheet popup | 2 |
302	| `/` | tmux-fzf keybinding picker | 2 |
303	
304	### Submenu rows
305	
306	Source of truth: `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-*.sh`.
307	
308	- **Layouts** (`L`): Even h/v (`1`/`2`), Main h/v (`3`/`4`), Tiled (`5`), Resize 75% (`+`), Pane h/j/k/l, Swap `{`/`}`.
309	- **Session** (`S`): Rename session/window (`$`/`,`), New session (`N`), Move window (`m`), Break pane (`r`), Link window (`K`), Renumber (`R`), Join marked here h/v (`j`/`J`), Send pane to (`s`), Kill pane/window/session/server (`x`/`W`/`X`/`Q`).
310	- **Sesh+** (`E`): TV picker (`V`), Built-in (`O`), Last sesh (`U`), scode here (`9`), CLI Tools tv (`B`).
311	- **Popups** (`o`): Lazygit (`g`), Shell (`s`), Floax scratchpad (`f`).
312	- **Theme** (`T`): Catppuccin (`c`), tmux2k (`t`).
313	- **System** (`Y`): Reload config (`R`), Install plugins (`I`), Update plugins (`U`), Detach (`d`), Clock (`k`).
314	
315	> **Hard cap**: the top menu is currently 14 rows at full height. Adding a 15th row will start failing on smaller terminals (mobile SSH, half-screen splits). Push lower-frequency items into a submenu instead, and re-test by shrinking the terminal vertically (heights 14 / 22 / 60).
316

```text
1	# tmux: nested display-menu via `run-shell` from a right-click parent menu is unreliable
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): submenu flashes and disappears, popup in bottom-right corner, `display-menu` flickers, right-click submenu won't stay open, tmux menu position wrong from status bar, submenu opens but selecting an item does nothing on second invocation
4	**First seen**: 2026-04
5	**Affects**: tmux 3.3+ (likely older too); any `display-menu` invoked indirectly via `run-shell "$HOME/.config/tmux/menu-foo.sh"` from a `MouseDown3*` parent
6	**Status**: workaround — inline the submenu items into the parent instead of nesting via shell script
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	A `tmux display-menu` submenu (e.g. `~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh`) behaves
11	two different ways depending on how it's invoked:
12	
13	- From a keyboard popup menu (e.g. `prefix + Enter` → "Layouts..."): opens
14	  near the cursor / pane center, stays open until an item is chosen. **Works.**
15	- From a **right-click status-bar** menu (e.g. right-click window tab →
16	  "Layouts..."): pops up in the **bottom-right corner of the terminal** and
17	  often **flashes away after a fraction of a second** before any item can be
18	  picked. Sometimes (if you happen to mouse over a row immediately) it stays.
19	
20	No error in `tmux show-messages`. The bind is correctly wired — `prefix +
21	Enter` path proves the script runs.
22	
23	## Root cause
24	
25	Two unrelated `display-menu` quirks stacked on top of each other:
26	
27	### 1. Mouse-release dismiss (the "flash and gone")
28	
29	A submenu without `-O` closes on the **next mouse event** that isn't a hover.
30	The right-click on the parent window-tab generated a pending mouse-release /
31	mouse-move event in tmux's event queue. The parent menu used `-O` (Open)
32	so it survived; the submenu didn't, so the queued release event hit it
33	immediately and dismissed it. With keyboard invocation there is no pending
34	mouse event, so the same submenu stayed open.
35	
36	### 2. `-x R -y P` from a status-bar event lands at bottom-right
37	
38	`-x R` = right edge of the pane. `-y P` = the line of the cursor's pane.
39	When `display-menu` is launched from a `MouseDown3Status` binding, "the
40	cursor's pane line" resolves to the **status bar row** (very bottom of the
41	terminal). Combined with `-x R` you get a popup glued to the bottom-right
42	corner. tmux 3.3+ then clamps it to fit on screen, which makes it look
43	"stuck" there. From a keyboard popup the cursor is in a normal pane, so the
44	same `-x R -y P` puts the menu in a sensible place near the parent.
45	
46	`man tmux` on `display-menu`:
47	> `M` for the mouse position, `W` for the window position on the status line,
48	> `S` for the line above or below the status line, `C` for the centre of the
49	> client.
50	
51	## Fix
52	
53	**Don't nest.** Inline the submenu items directly into the parent menu, even
54	if it pushes the parent above the ~14-row soft cap (see
55	`AGENTS.md` → "tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu"). The cap exists for a
56	real reason (small terminals silently suppress oversized menus), so when
57	inlining grows the parent past 14 rows, drop the lowest-frequency rows and
58	move them to the keyboard popup (`prefix + Enter` → submenu) where the
59	nesting works fine.
60	
61	```tmux
62	# Bad: nested via run-shell (selection silently no-ops on 2nd invocation)
63	bind-key -n MouseDown3Status display-menu -O ... \
64	  "Layouts..." L { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh" } \
65	  ...
66	
67	# Good: inline the layout commands directly
68	bind-key -n MouseDown3Status display-menu -O ... \
69	  "Even horizontal" 1 { select-layout even-horizontal } \
70	  "Even vertical"   2 { select-layout even-vertical } \
71	  "Tiled (grid)"    5 { select-layout tiled } \
72	  ...
73	```
74	
75	The keyboard popup path (`prefix + Enter` → "Layouts..." → `run-shell
76	~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh`) keeps working — the bug is specific to
77	mouse-driven parents whose mouse-event lifecycle interferes with the child
78	menu's input handling.
79	
80	## Things that look like fixes but aren't
81	
82	Spent time trying these — none worked reliably across "first invocation"
83	vs "after cancelling once":
84	
85	- `-O` on the submenu: stops the immediate flash-and-gone, but on second
86	  invocation after cancelling the parent, selecting an item silently
87	  no-ops.
88	- `-x M -y M` on the submenu: fixes the bottom-right placement, but mouse
89	  position state is stale after cancel-and-retry, so it pops up in
90	  unpredictable places.
91	- `run-shell -d 0.1 "~/.config/tmux/menu-foo.sh"`: deferring the shell
92	  exec lets the parent's mouse-release drain, fixes the flash, but the
93	  selection-no-ops bug remains.
94	- `display-popup` wrapping the submenu: changes mouse semantics entirely
95	  but you lose `display-menu`'s key shortcuts.
96	
97	The man page (tmux 3.3+) explains why `-O` alone isn't enough:
98	
99	> If the mouse is enabled and the menu is opened from a mouse key binding,
100	> releasing the mouse button … closes the menu. `-M` tells tmux the menu
101	> should handle mouse events; by default only menus opened from mouse key
102	> bindings do so.
103	
104	A submenu launched via `run-shell` is NOT considered "opened from a mouse
105	key binding" — so `-M` doesn't help either, and the trailing mouse events
106	from the now-defunct parent leak into an undefined input state for the
107	child.
108	
109	## Related
110	
111	- `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` — different silent failure mode
112	  for the same `display-menu` command (height clamping / menu-too-tall).
113
```

```text
1	# tmux display-menu silently doesn't open (no error, no menu)
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- `prefix + <key>` bound to `display-menu` does nothing — no popup, no error message, no entry in `tmux show-messages`
5	- `tmux list-keys -T prefix <key>` shows the binding correctly
6	- Other bindings on the same key (e.g. `bind-key … display-message`) fire fine
7	- Right-click pane menus and other simpler `display-menu` invocations still work
8	- Menu opens on a tall terminal, fails on a short one — or works after deleting half the rows
9	- Bisecting a long flat menu by halving the rows reveals the failure depends on **menu length**, not on the bound key (the key was a red herring)
10	
11	**First seen**: 2026-04
12	**Affects**: tmux 3.6a (likely all 3.x), any platform
13	**Status**: workaround documented (script-driven menu with height-aware tier trimming)
14	
15	## Symptom
16	
17	Bound a 50-row `display-menu` to `prefix + Space`, then to `prefix + Enter`, then to `prefix + e`. Each new key would also "not work" — no popup, no error, no log entry. Hours of debugging key encoding (`extended-keys`, `csi-u`, Ghostty `macos-option-as-alt`, upstream tmux/tmux issues #4571 #4147 #4959 #4984) all turned up nothing because **the keys were bound correctly all along**. The actual failure was that the menu was taller than the terminal.
18	
19	Reproduction:
20	
21	```tmux
22	# Bind a long menu (50+ rows) and shrink the terminal vertically.
23	# Above some height threshold: menu opens.
24	# Below it: prefix + key does nothing. No error.
25	bind-key Space display-menu -T 'big' -x R -y P \
26	  "Row 1" 1 "display-message 1" \
27	  "Row 2" 2 "display-message 2" \
28	  ... 50 more rows ...
29	```
30	
31	This is documented behaviour buried in `man tmux`:
32	
33	> If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed.
34	
35	It also applies in a less obvious way at moderate heights when `-y P` (anchor to status bar) leaves no room above.
36	
37	## Confounding "real but smaller" bugs
38	
39	Bisecting the failing menu surfaced two genuine quoting bugs that **also** broke the menu but were not the root cause of the dominant symptom:
40	
41	1. **`'\;'` as an accelerator key** — tmux stored this as bare `\;` in the binding, then at menu-execution time interpreted it as a command separator, ending `display-menu` early. Subsequent menu rows became arguments to `last-pane`, producing `command last-pane: too many arguments (need at most 0)` — visible in `tmux show-messages` only when the binding was rebuilt, not on every keypress. **Fix**: use a different accelerator key (`P` instead of `'\;'` for "Last pane").
42	2. **`fzf-tmux ... --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})'` inline in a menu row** — fzf's `{2..}` range syntax collides with tmux's command-block delimiters `{ }`, silently aborting parse of that row. **Fix**: extract complex commands into shell scripts (no nested-quote disasters in a real shell).
43	
44	Both fixes are necessary but neither restored the menu by itself; the dominant cause was always menu-too-tall.
45	
46	## Root cause
47	
48	`display-menu` does not paginate. tmux measures the rendered popup height; if it exceeds available terminal height (after `status-position` and `-y` anchor offset), the popup is suppressed entirely with no log message. There is no scroll, no truncation, no error event.
49	
50	Why this is hard to diagnose:
51	- A static config + a tall terminal means it works "always" → no one notices the limit until they ssh in from a small pane / mobile shell / split layout.
52	- Adding rows over time keeps it working until one row tips it over → looks like "the new row broke something".
53	- Bisecting a long menu by halving the rows works (because the half is short enough to render) → looks like a content problem.
54	
55	## Workaround
56	
57	Two changes:
58	
59	1. **Generate the menu from a script** that reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list:
60	   - Tier 0 (always): ~7 highest-frequency rows
61	   - Tier 1 (height ≥ 22): adds new-window/split/zoom
62	   - Tier 2 (height ≥ 14): adds submenu launchers + cheatsheet/key-search
63	2. **Push everything else into submenus**, each implemented as its own `tmux display-menu` script. Submenus get a fresh quoting context, so nested escaping disasters go away.
64	
65	Layout in this repo:
66	
67	```
68	~/.config/tmux/menu.sh           # top menu (tier-aware)
69	~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh   # → Layouts submenu
70	~/.config/tmux/menu-session.sh   # → Session mgmt submenu
71	~/.config/tmux/menu-sesh.sh      # → Sesh extras submenu
72	~/.config/tmux/menu-popups.sh    # → Popups submenu
73	~/.config/tmux/menu-theme.sh     # → Theme submenu
74	~/.config/tmux/menu-system.sh    # → System submenu (reload, plugins, detach, clock)
75	~/.config/tmux/sesh-picker.sh    # nested fzf-tmux extracted out
76	~/.config/tmux/sesh-windows.sh   # nested fzf-tmux extracted out
77	```
78	
79	Bindings in `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`:
80	
81	```tmux
82	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
83	bind-key e     run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
84	```
85	
86	When adding a new menu item, add it to the relevant submenu, not the top menu. Top-menu cap is ~14 rows (fits a 20-row terminal). When adding a row that contains `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, or more than two levels of nested quotes, extract to a script.
87	
88	## Prevention
89	
90	When designing a tmux popup menu:
91	
92	1. **Cap the top menu at ~14 rows.** Use submenus (separate `display-menu` scripts) for everything else.
93	2. **Generate the menu from a script** that consults `#{client_height}` and `#{client_width}` if you want auto-trim across many heights.
94	3. **Verify by shrinking the terminal vertically.** A "menu works" smoke test on a full-height window does not catch this.
95	4. **Don't blame key encoding first.** If a `display-menu` binding doesn't fire, bind the same `display-menu` to a known-good letter key on a known-tall terminal — if it works there, the problem is height (or content), not the key.
96	5. **For complex commands inside menu rows** (any `{`, `}`, `;`, backtick, nested fzf binds): extract to a script.
97	
98	## Related
99	
100	- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu.sh` — top-level menu generator (height-aware)
101	- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-*.sh` — submenu scripts
102	- `dot_config/tmux/executable_sesh-picker.sh`, `executable_sesh-windows.sh` — extracted complex commands
103	- `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` — `bind-key Space` / `bind-key e` → `menu.sh`
104	- [`AGENTS.md` → Tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu](../AGENTS.md) — adjacent invariant about a different `display-menu` failure mode (off-screen on tmux 3.2a). The 3.3+ position-clamping fix doesn't help with menu-too-tall — that limit is independent.
105	- `man tmux` → `display-menu` → "If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."
106
```

12	| [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) | — | all bind-keys and popup menu |
13	| [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf) | — | default theme (top status bar) |
14	| [`dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf) | — | alternative theme (bottom status bar) |
15	| [`dot_config/tmux/executable_responsive.sh`](../../../dot_config/tmux/executable_responsive.sh) | `~/.config/tmux/responsive.sh` | responsive status bar for Catppuccin |
16	
17	This setup is tuned for coding-agent and Neovim workflows:
18	
19	- native popup menu on `prefix + Space`; script-driven (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) with submenus and height-aware tier trimming — see [keybindings.md](./keybindings.md#popup-menu-prefix--space)
20	- fuzzy keybinding search on `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf, replaces the built-in list-keys dump)
21	- markdown cheatsheet via `prefix + Space` → `?` (rendered with `glow`)
22	- floating scratchpad on `prefix + F` (tmux-floax, persistent), one-shot popup shell on `prefix + \``, lazygit popup on `prefix + G`
23	- Catppuccin (default, top status bar) or tmux2k (bottom) — switchable at runtime
24	- Catppuccin status bar is responsive — modules adapt to terminal width (mobile-friendly)
25	- vim-style pane navigation and copy mode
26	- URL opening via fzf (`prefix + u`) and tmux-open in copy mode
27	- capture pane to clipboard helpers
28	- sesh integration for session picking
29	- `extended-keys` with `csi-u` so keys like `Ctrl+/` reach Neovim inside tmux
30	- OSC 52 clipboard and OSC passthrough enabled
31	- macOS terminal must send Option as Meta for `M-` bindings — see [ghostty.md](../ghostty.md)
32	
33	## In this folder
34	
35	- [keybindings.md](./keybindings.md) — all keybindings and the popup menu
36	- [themes.md](./themes.md) — Catppuccin / tmux2k selection, switching, troubleshooting
37	- [vim.md](./vim.md) — tmux × Vim/Neovim notes and external resources
38	
39	## First-time setup
40	
41	After `chezmoi apply`, start tmux and run `prefix + I` once to let TPM install the plugins. The theme files also auto-clone their plugin on first source as a safety net, but TPM is the canonical installer.
42	
43	## Version requirement: tmux >= 3.3
44	
45	The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space`) is generated by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh` and uses `display-menu -x R -y P`. Two distinct failure modes drove the current design:
46	
47	1. **Position clamping (tmux 3.3+ required).** On tmux 3.2a (shipped by Ubuntu 22.04 apt) the menu is positioned past the terminal's right edge and silently suppressed. tmux 3.3 introduced position clamping and arithmetic in `-x`/`-y`, so the menu renders correctly. The man page explicitly states _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_
48	2. **Menu-too-tall is a separate failure mode.** `display-menu` does not paginate. Even on tmux 3.6+, a 50-row flat menu silently fails to open on terminals shorter than ~50 lines (mobile SSH, half-screen splits, etc.) — no error, no log entry. Fixed by the script-driven, height-tiered approach: the script reads `#{client_height}` and emits one of three tier sets so the top menu never exceeds ~14 rows. Lower-frequency items moved into submenus. Full debugging story: [`pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`](../../../pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
49	
50	The ansible `devtools` role now checks the tmux version and, when it is below 3.3, upgrades automatically:
51	
52	1. **Linuxbrew present** → `brew install tmux` (latest stable).
53	2. **No Linuxbrew, x86_64 Linux** → download [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage), extract to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/squashfs-root/` (no FUSE needed), and install a shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux` that exec's the bundled binary. `~/.local/bin` sits ahead of `/usr/bin` in PATH so the newer binary wins.
54	3. **No Linuxbrew, non-x86_64** (e.g. armv7l, aarch64 servers without brew) → ansible prints a warning; build from source or enable Linuxbrew.
55	
56	### Switching a running server to the new binary
57	
58	After an upgrade, existing tmux servers keep running the old binary (a live process doesn't re-exec on PATH change). Clients attaching to the same socket also stay on the old version. To switch over:
59	
60	```bash
61	# lose current sessions but get a clean 3.3+ server
62	tmux kill-server
63	
64	# or: start the new server on a new socket and migrate sessions manually
65	tmux -L new new-session -s work
66	```
67	
68	Verify with `tmux -V` (binary version) and, inside tmux, `#{version}` in a format string (server version).
69	
70	### Terminfo (`missing or unsuitable terminal`)
71	
72	If `tmux attach` fails with `missing or unsuitable terminal: <name>`, the host is missing the terminfo entry for whatever `$TERM` your outer terminal advertises (common on minimal Ubuntu installs, Docker images, and freshly provisioned servers — base ncurses ships only `xterm`, `vt100`, `linux`, …).
73	
74	On Debian/Ubuntu the `devtools` role now installs [`ncurses-term`](https://packages.ubuntu.com/jammy/ncurses-term) alongside the tmux baseline, which adds entries for `tmux-256color`, `alacritty`, `ghostty`, `rxvt-unicode-256color`, `screen-256color`, and friends. macOS ships the extended catalog by default.
75	
76	Fallbacks if you can't install the package (e.g. `noRoot` mode on a locked-down host):
77	
78	```bash
79	# quick test — pick a terminfo that's already present
80	TERM=xterm-256color tmux a
81	
82	# user-local install: copy your local terminfo entry over SSH
83	infocmp -x | ssh remote -- tic -x -
84	# lands in ~/.terminfo/, no sudo needed
85	```
86	
87	## OSC 52 Clipboard (SSH-friendly yank)
88	
89	Full cross-layer explainer (terminal ↔ tmux ↔ Neovim ↔ `x` CLI): see [**clipboard.md**](../clipboard.md). Summary of what tmux contributes:
90	
91	`set-clipboard on` + `allow-passthrough on` in [`common.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf) let tmux relay OSC 52 escape sequences from inner TUIs to the outer terminal emulator, so yanks reach the local machine's clipboard even over SSH. The same file declares the `clipboard` terminal-feature for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, and `alacritty*` so tmux doesn't need a `Ms` entry in terminfo to emit OSC 52.
92	
93	The capture-pane helpers (`prefix + y` / `Y` / `C-y` in [`keybindings.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf)) pipe through `tmux load-buffer -w -` rather than `pbcopy`/`xclip`, so they also work over SSH (the `-w` flag tells tmux to forward the buffer via OSC 52 alongside the paste buffer).
94	
95	The Neovim side is paired in [`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`](../../../dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua): when `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY` is set, `vim.g.clipboard` is overridden to `vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` (builtin since Neovim 0.10). Local sessions keep the default `pbcopy`/`xclip` provider so paste still works.
96	
97	### Verify it's wired up
98	
99	```bash
100	# tmux should report clipboard support for the current client
```

## Investigation Summary

Your right-click menu disappearing at the bottom of the screen is a **known tmux design issue** with menu positioning. Here are the exact sources:

### 1. Right-Click Pane Menu Binding
**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` **Lines 12–39**

The pane right-click uses:
```tmux
bind-key -n MouseDown3Pane \
  if-shell -F -t = "#{||:#{mouse_any_flag},#{&&:#{pane_in_mode},#{?#{m/r:(copy|view)-mode,#{pane_mode}},0,1}}}" \
    { select-pane -t = ; send-keys -M } \
    { display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{pane_current_command} (pane #{pane_index})" -t = -x M -y M \
        ... 30+ menu items ...
```

**Key issue:** `-x M -y M` — both coordinates are anchored to the **mouse position**. When you right-click near the bottom, `M` resolves to a low y-coordinate, and tmux's auto-clamping in 3.3+ may suppress the entire menu if it would extend past the terminal height.

**Window-tab menu** (line 55) uses `-x W -y W` (window position), and **session menu** (line 77) uses `-x M -y W` (mixed anchors).

### 2. Known Menu Positioning Bug
**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md`

Documents two distinct failures:
- **Mouse-release dismiss:** nested submenus flash and disappear because pending mouse events from the parent right-click dismiss them (even with `-O` flag).
- **Bottom-right corner placement:** `-y P` (pane line) from a status-bar event resolves to the status bar row (bottom of terminal), gluing the menu to bottom-right.

**Workaround applied in your config:** Lines 44–50 of `keybindings.conf` explicitly inline all layout commands into the window-tab menu instead of nesting via `run-shell`, to avoid this exact bug.

### 3. Menu-Too-Tall Silent Suppression
**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`

- **Root cause:** `display-menu` silently suppresses the entire popup if menu height exceeds available terminal height after `status-position` and `-y` offset. No error, no log entry — "if the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed" per `man tmux`.
- **Your config workaround:** `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh` reads `#{client_height}` and emits three tiers (14 rows max for top menu) so it always fits even on mobile SSH.

### 4. Version Constraint & AppImage
**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` **Lines 1884–2000+**

- **Minimum tmux version:** 3.3 (line 1925: `tmux_min_version: "3.3"`)
- **Reason:** tmux 3.2a silently suppresses menus positioned past terminal right edge; 3.3 introduced position clamping and arithmetic in `-x`/`-y`.
- **AppImage fallback:** If Linuxbrew unavailable on x86_64, downloads `nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage` and installs a shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux`.

### 5. Documentation
**File:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md` **Lines 149–161**

Explicitly states the pane menu uses `display-menu -O` so it stays open after mouse release (tmux defaults omit `-O` and dismiss immediately, making right-click menus "unusable").

---

**Diagnosis for your bug:** When right-clicking near the bottom, `-x M -y M` places the menu anchor at the mouse (low y). If the 30-row pane menu would extend below the terminal, tmux 3.3+ clamps it, but the bottom-pinned anchor may cause the menu to render off-screen or collapse. Check: (1) terminal height `echo $LINES`, (2) tmux version `tmux -V`, (3) try right-clicking higher where there's more space below the click point.

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md`

```text
1	# tmux: nested display-menu via `run-shell` from a right-click parent menu is unreliable
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): submenu flashes and disappears, popup in bottom-right corner, `display-menu` flickers, right-click submenu won't stay open, tmux menu position wrong from status bar, submenu opens but selecting an item does nothing on second invocation
4	**First seen**: 2026-04
5	**Affects**: tmux 3.3+ (likely older too); any `display-menu` invoked indirectly via `run-shell "$HOME/.config/tmux/menu-foo.sh"` from a `MouseDown3*` parent
6	**Status**: workaround — inline the submenu items into the parent instead of nesting via shell script
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	A `tmux display-menu` submenu (e.g. `~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh`) behaves
11	two different ways depending on how it's invoked:
12	
13	- From a keyboard popup menu (e.g. `prefix + Enter` → "Layouts..."): opens
14	  near the cursor / pane center, stays open until an item is chosen. **Works.**
15	- From a **right-click status-bar** menu (e.g. right-click window tab →
16	  "Layouts..."): pops up in the **bottom-right corner of the terminal** and
17	  often **flashes away after a fraction of a second** before any item can be
18	  picked. Sometimes (if you happen to mouse over a row immediately) it stays.
19	
20	No error in `tmux show-messages`. The bind is correctly wired — `prefix +
21	Enter` path proves the script runs.
22	
23	## Root cause
24	
25	Two unrelated `display-menu` quirks stacked on top of each other:
26	
27	### 1. Mouse-release dismiss (the "flash and gone")
28	
29	A submenu without `-O` closes on the **next mouse event** that isn't a hover.
30	The right-click on the parent window-tab generated a pending mouse-release /
31	mouse-move event in tmux's event queue. The parent menu used `-O` (Open)
32	so it survived; the submenu didn't, so the queued release event hit it
33	immediately and dismissed it. With keyboard invocation there is no pending
34	mouse event, so the same submenu stayed open.
35	
36	### 2. `-x R -y P` from a status-bar event lands at bottom-right
37	
38	`-x R` = right edge of the pane. `-y P` = the line of the cursor's pane.
39	When `display-menu` is launched from a `MouseDown3Status` binding, "the
40	cursor's pane line" resolves to the **status bar row** (very bottom of the
41	terminal). Combined with `-x R` you get a popup glued to the bottom-right
42	corner. tmux 3.3+ then clamps it to fit on screen, which makes it look
43	"stuck" there. From a keyboard popup the cursor is in a normal pane, so the
44	same `-x R -y P` puts the menu in a sensible place near the parent.
45	
46	`man tmux` on `display-menu`:
47	> `M` for the mouse position, `W` for the window position on the status line,
48	> `S` for the line above or below the status line, `C` for the centre of the
49	> client.
50	
51	## Fix
52	
53	**Don't nest.** Inline the submenu items directly into the parent menu, even
54	if it pushes the parent above the ~14-row soft cap (see
55	`AGENTS.md` → "tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu"). The cap exists for a
56	real reason (small terminals silently suppress oversized menus), so when
57	inlining grows the parent past 14 rows, drop the lowest-frequency rows and
58	move them to the keyboard popup (`prefix + Enter` → submenu) where the
59	nesting works fine.
60	
61	```tmux
62	# Bad: nested via run-shell (selection silently no-ops on 2nd invocation)
63	bind-key -n MouseDown3Status display-menu -O ... \
64	  "Layouts..." L { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh" } \
65	  ...
66	
67	# Good: inline the layout commands directly
68	bind-key -n MouseDown3Status display-menu -O ... \
69	  "Even horizontal" 1 { select-layout even-horizontal } \
70	  "Even vertical"   2 { select-layout even-vertical } \
71	  "Tiled (grid)"    5 { select-layout tiled } \
72	  ...
73	```
74	
75	The keyboard popup path (`prefix + Enter` → "Layouts..." → `run-shell
76	~/.config/tmux/menu-layouts.sh`) keeps working — the bug is specific to
77	mouse-driven parents whose mouse-event lifecycle interferes with the child
78	menu's input handling.
79	
80	## Things that look like fixes but aren't
81	
82	Spent time trying these — none worked reliably across "first invocation"
83	vs "after cancelling once":
84	
85	- `-O` on the submenu: stops the immediate flash-and-gone, but on second
86	  invocation after cancelling the parent, selecting an item silently
87	  no-ops.
88	- `-x M -y M` on the submenu: fixes the bottom-right placement, but mouse
89	  position state is stale after cancel-and-retry, so it pops up in
90	  unpredictable places.
91	- `run-shell -d 0.1 "~/.config/tmux/menu-foo.sh"`: deferring the shell
92	  exec lets the parent's mouse-release drain, fixes the flash, but the
93	  selection-no-ops bug remains.
94	- `display-popup` wrapping the submenu: changes mouse semantics entirely
95	  but you lose `display-menu`'s key shortcuts.
96	
97	The man page (tmux 3.3+) explains why `-O` alone isn't enough:
98	
99	> If the mouse is enabled and the menu is opened from a mouse key binding,
100	> releasing the mouse button … closes the menu. `-M` tells tmux the menu
101	> should handle mouse events; by default only menus opened from mouse key
102	> bindings do so.
103	
104	A submenu launched via `run-shell` is NOT considered "opened from a mouse
105	key binding" — so `-M` doesn't help either, and the trailing mouse events
106	from the now-defunct parent leak into an undefined input state for the
107	child.
108	
109	## Related
110	
111	- `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` — different silent failure mode
112	  for the same `display-menu` command (height clamping / menu-too-tall).
113
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3	#
4	# Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5	#   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6	#      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7	#      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8	#   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9	#      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10	#      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11	#      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12	#   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13	#      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14	#
15	# Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16	#   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17	#   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh, menu-agents.sh
18	#
19	# See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24	DIR=~/.config/tmux
25	
26	# Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27	declare -a tier0=(
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29	  "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30	  ""             ""  ""
31	  "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32	  "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33	  "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34	  ""             ""  ""
35	  "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36	  "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37	)
38	
39	# Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40	declare -a tier1=(
41	  ""             ""  ""
42	  "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43	  "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44	  "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45	  "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46	)
47	
48	# Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49	declare -a tier2=(
50	  ""             ""  ""
51	  "→ Layouts"    L   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-layouts.sh'"
52	  "→ Session"    S   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-session.sh'"
53	  "→ Sesh+"      E   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-sesh.sh'"
54	  "→ Agents"     A   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-agents.sh'"
55	  "→ Popups"     o   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-popups.sh'"
56	  "→ Theme"      T   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-theme.sh'"
57	  "→ System"     Y   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-system.sh'"
58	  ""             ""  ""
59	  "Cheatsheet"   "?" "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' 'glow -p $DIR/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null || less $DIR/cheatsheet.md'"
60	  "Search keys"  "/" "run-shell -b ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/scripts/keybinding.sh"
61	)
62	
63	rows=("${tier0[@]}")
64	if [ "$H" -ge 22 ]; then
65	  rows+=("${tier1[@]}" "${tier2[@]}")
66	elif [ "$H" -ge 14 ]; then
67	  rows+=("${tier2[@]}")
68	fi
69	
70	exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux (h=$H)" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"
71

# Fix: tmux right-click pane menu flashes and disappears near screen bottom

## Context

When right-clicking on a pane in the **upper portion** of the screen, the
pane context menu (`MouseDown3Pane`) appears and stays open as expected.
When right-clicking on a pane in the **lower portion** of the screen, the
menu briefly appears and then disappears within a frame — unusable.

### Root cause

The binding at `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf:13-39` invokes
`display-menu -O -T "..." -t = -x M -y M ...` with **23 visible rows**
(17 items + 5 separators + 1 title) plus tmux's borders ≈ **25 rows of
total menu height**.

`-y M` anchors the **top-left** corner of the menu at the mouse cursor
position. When `mouse_y + 25 > client_height`, the menu would extend
past the bottom of the terminal. tmux 3.3+ tries to clamp it upward to
fit, but the clamp interaction with the queued `MouseDown3` /
`MouseUp3` event leaks dismisses the menu before the user can interact
— observed as the "flash and gone" symptom.

This is **distinct** from the silent-suppression failure mode
documented in `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (which is
"menu never appears at all" because total menu height > terminal
height). Here the menu *can* fit on the terminal as a whole; it just
can't fit *below* the click point.

### Why we cannot use the existing tier-trim pattern

`menu.sh` solves a different problem (terminal too small overall, not
position-relative). Tier-trimming would help only on small terminals,
not on 50-60 row terminals where the user is clicking near the bottom.

### Why we cannot extract to a `run-shell` script

`pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md` documents that any
`display-menu` invoked indirectly via `run-shell` from a `MouseDown3*`
binding loses its "opened from a mouse key binding" status, so `-M`
becomes a no-op and trailing mouse events from the parent leak into
the child. The current binding **must** stay inline with `display-menu`
in `keybindings.conf`.

### Why we cannot use `-y S` / `-y C`

`-y S` (status line) or `-y C` (centre of client) would always place
the menu at a fixed location, losing the cursor-following UX that
makes the right-click menu feel native. The user explicitly noted that
when there is enough space, the menu position is correct — so
preserving cursor-following is a goal.

### Intended outcome

Right-clicking anywhere on the pane should open the menu in a stable,
fully-visible position:

- Above the click point (when there's space) — unchanged behaviour.
- **Below the click point (when within ~25 rows of the bottom) — menu
  opens *above* the cursor instead of getting clamped/flashed.**

## Approach

Replace the static `-y M` with a tmux format expression that picks the
anchor row conditionally on `#{mouse_y}` and `#{client_height}`:

\```tmux
-y "#{?#{e|>:#{e|+:#{mouse_y},#{T:@menu_height_pane}},#{client_height}},#{e|-:#{mouse_y},#{T:@menu_height_pane}},#{mouse_y}}"
\```

Translation:

> If `mouse_y + menu_height > client_height` (menu would overflow
> downward), anchor the menu at `mouse_y - menu_height` (so the
> bottom of the menu lands at the click point and the menu opens
> *upward*). Otherwise anchor at `mouse_y` (default behaviour).

The menu height is stored as a tmux user option `@menu_height_pane`
set near the top of the binding section, with a comment that ties its
value to the visible-row count of the menu so it can be kept in sync
when items are added/removed.

### Why a tmux user option, not a hardcoded literal

The literal `25` would work but rots silently — the next person to
add or remove a menu row will not realise the anchor math depends on
it. A `set -g @menu_height_pane "25"` line directly above the binding
puts the constant near the menu definition with a comment, and lets us
reference it by name from the format string. This mirrors the
"document the soft cap inline" pattern already used for the window-tab
menu's row count comment at `keybindings.conf:44-53`.

### Cursor-outside-menu after upward repositioning

When the menu opens upward, the cursor will be **just below the
menu's bottom edge**. The binding already uses `-O` (Open), so a
mouse-release at that location does NOT dismiss the menu (this is what
`-O` is for). The user moves the mouse up into the menu to interact —
identical UX to right-clicking near the bottom of any modern GUI app.
No change needed to `-O` or any other flag.

## Critical files

- **`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`** (lines 12-39) — the only
  file modified. Add `set -g @menu_height_pane "25"` directly above
  the `MouseDown3Pane` binding (with a comment block explaining how to
  recompute it when items change), then replace `-y M` with the
  conditional format expression above.

## Notes / non-goals

- **Window-tab menu (`MouseDown3Status`, lines 54-73)** uses `-y W`
  (window position on the status line) and is anchored to the status
  bar, not the cursor — it does not exhibit this bug. No change.
- **Session menu (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`, lines 76-86)** uses
  `-y W` for the same reason. No change.
- **`menu.sh` and submenu scripts** — no change. They use `-y P`
  (top of pane) or `-y W` (status), neither of which has this issue.
- We are NOT trimming the pane menu. All 17 items stay; only the
  positioning logic changes.
- We are NOT changing `-x M` — horizontal clamping in tmux 3.3+
  works fine and the menu's width (~40 cols) rarely overflows.

## Verification

After running `chezmoi apply` and reloading tmux config
(`tmux source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` or `prefix + R` if
bound):

1. **Upper-screen behaviour (regression check)** — split a window so
   the top pane is large. Right-click in row 5-10 of the pane. The
   menu should appear with its top-left at the cursor, identical to
   current behaviour.

2. **Lower-screen behaviour (the fix)** — in the same large pane,
   right-click in the **bottom 25 rows** (e.g. row 55 of a 60-row
   terminal). The menu should now appear with its **bottom-left at
   the cursor** (i.e. the menu opens upward), and stay open.

3. **Edge case: tall menu vs short terminal** — shrink the terminal
   to 30 rows (smaller than the menu's 25-row height + a few rows
   margin). Right-click anywhere. tmux's clamping will still adjust
   the position; menu should be visible somewhere on screen and stay
   open. (If menu height ≥ terminal height entirely, the documented
   silent-suppression behaviour from
   `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` still applies — that
   is out of scope for this fix.)

4. **Other right-click menus (regression check)** — right-click on a
   window tab in the status bar, and on the session name on the left
   of the status bar. Both should behave identically to before the
   change (they were never affected).

5. **Submenu interactions (regression check)** — from the pane
   right-click menu, trigger items that themselves open prompts /
   `choose-tree` (e.g. "Send pane to window..." → `S`, "Rename
   window"). Confirm the inner UI still appears and is responsive.

```

Reverted. Original `-y M` should work as before. Now let me diagnose the regression and design a better fix.

**Root cause of my failed fix**: `-y M` is *not* the same as `-y "#{mouse_y}"`. tmux's `M` token is special-cased — it places the menu so the cursor lands **inside** the menu's interactive area (on the title row, per your observation). Substituting raw `#{mouse_y}` shifted the menu by one row, putting the cursor on the border — which is why the upper-screen menu started flash-dismissing too (cursor outside interactive area = mouse-release escapes the menu).

The correct fix is to use tmux's documented `M-N` / `M+N` offset syntax (per `man tmux` display-menu: *"The position may be followed by an offset, for example M+1 or W-2"*). Let me verify it works under format expansion before re-applying.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-28 05:21:24Z)**_

Cleaned up and recounted: **24 rows total** (21 items including the multi-line "Send pane to window" and "Break to new window", + title + 2 borders).

**Diagnosis of why v1 broke**:

1. **Position offset (middle-click feels wrong)**: tmux's `-y M` token is special-cased — it places the menu so the **title** sits at the cursor (one row above where `-y "#{mouse_y}"` would put it). My substitution shifted the entire menu down by one row.

2. **Top-click flashing**: that one-row shift moved the cursor out of the menu's interactive area onto the border, so mouse-release escaped the menu and dismissed it (even though `-O` is set).

3. **The crash**: most likely caused by the format engine re-evaluating `#{mouse_y}` during tmux's clamp re-render — a stale/invalid value in that path could trip tmux. The fix below avoids this by using `M-N` arithmetic inside tmux (not via format engine).

**Proposed v2** — use tmux's documented `-y M-N` offset syntax (`man tmux`: *"The position may be followed by an offset, for example M+1 or W-2"*):

```tmux
-y "#{?#{e|>:#{e|+:#{mouse_y},#{@menu_height_pane}},#{client_height}},M-#{@menu_height_pane},M}"
```

The conditional emits either the literal string `"M-25"` or `"M"`. tmux then handles the offset internally — `mouse_y` is only read once at menu-open, never during re-render. In the fits-below branch the value is plain `M`, so middle-screen clicks behave **identically to before** (title at cursor).

The unavoidable trade-off when the menu flips upward: cursor lands just below the menu's bottom border. `-O` keeps it open; user moves mouse up into the menu to select.

Want me to:
- **(A)** apply v2 (smart positioning, with the upward-flip trade-off), or
- **(B)** skip smart positioning entirely and trim the pane menu to ~14 items so it always fits at `-y M` no matter where you click (drops less-used items like Mark/Swap-marked, Join-h/v, Send-pane-to-window, Break-to-window — these are still reachable via `prefix + Space` popup), or
- **(C)** stay with the revert and accept the bottom-of-screen flash as a minor quirk?
